sections.overview: The Red-throated Loon is a circumpolar Arctic breeder that winters mainly along northern coasts.
sections.identification: It is the smallest and slimmest loon regularly seen in France; breeding adults show a narrow rusty throat patch and a fine, slightly upturned bill.
sections.habitat: It nests beside small freshwater ponds in tundra or taiga, then moves to bays, estuaries and sheltered coastal waters for winter.
sections.diet: Fish form most of its food, although it also takes crustaceans, molluscs and aquatic insects.
sections.behavior: It watches with its head partly submerged, then dives smoothly to pursue prey underwater.
sections.reproduction: Pairs usually lay two eggs in a simple nest close to water, and both adults incubate them for about 27 days.
sections.ecology: Unlike loons that depend on large lakes, this species can breed on small tundra ponds and feed in larger waters some distance away. ADW also describes nests close to water.
sections.conservation: Its global Red List category is Least Concern, but the LPO notes a declining trend and pressures including pollution, disturbance and climate change.
